SUBJECT:                     SUMMARY OF MARCH 17, 2026, PRE-APPLICATION
                             MEETING WITH KAIROS ON HERMES 2 PRECAST
                             CONCRETE FOR SAFETY-RELATED STRUCTURES AND
                             EXTREME WIND DESIGN CRITERIA

Meeting Information:

Applicant: Kairos Power LLC (Kairos)

Project Nos.: 05000611 and 05000612

Meeting Type: Partially Closed Meeting

Public Meeting Notice: Agencywide Documents Access and Management System (ADAMS)
Accession No.: ML26055A310

Applicant Presentation Slides: ML26070A199

Contact: Samuel Cuadrado, OAR/DARL
         (301) 415-2946
 M. Hayes                                         2



Meeting Summary:
Public Session
On March 17, 2026, a partially closed meeting was held between the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC) staff and representatives of Kairos Power, LLC (Kairos). The purpose of the
meeting was to discuss the use of precast concrete for safety-related structures and the design
criteria for extreme winds for the Kairos Power Fluoride Salt-Cooled, High Temperature Non-Power
Reactor (Hermes 2).
During the public session of the meeting Kairos and the NRC staff discussed the extreme wind
design criteria and precast concrete for Hermes 2 as follows:
Extreme Wind Design Criteria
•   Kairos stated that the Hermes 2 Preliminary Safety Analysis Report (PSAR) (ML23151A743)
    references RG 1.76, “Design-Basis Tornado and Tornado Missiles for Nuclear Power Plants,”
    Revision 1, and RG 1.221, “Design-Basis Hurricane and Hurricane Missiles for Nuclear Power
    Plants,” for tornado and hurricane protection of Hermes 2’s two safety-related reactor buildings.
    The reactor buildings will be designed to the principal design criteria (PDC) described in the
    PSAR; however, the design basis is being updated and the Final Safety Analysis Report (FSAR)
    will use the criteria from the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) guideline
    document FEMA P-361, “Safe Rooms for Tornadoes and Hurricanes: Guidance for Community
    and Residential Safe Rooms,” 2024, for tornado and hurricane design of the safety-related
    superstructure.
•   Kairos stated that FEMA P-361 uses the International Code Council (ICC) standard, ICC-500,
    “ICC/NSSA Standard for the Design and Construction of Storm Shelters,” as a reference
    standard. Kairos also stated that the ICC-500 standard is referenced by the international
    building code where storm shelters are required.
•   Kairos stated that Hermes 2 relies on a functional containment. As such, the safety-related
    building is not designed as a physical containment for fission product retention like other
    reactors but still provides protection to safety related structures systems and components
    (SSCs) from the effects of natural phenomena and external event hazards.
•   In its presentation slides 17 through 23, Kairos listed the sections from FEMA P-361 that apply
    to Hermes 2 and for each one provided a technical justification for its use.
•   The staff stated that based on the information presented at this time it didn’t have any red flags
    or significant concerns with the approach.
Precast Concrete
•   Kairos stated that per the Hermes 2 PSAR, the safety-related portion of the reactor building is a
    hybrid of cast in place and precast concrete structural elements.
•   Kairos stated that the Hermes 2 design will use emulative precast concrete for safety-related
    reactor building structure designed per the American Concrete Institute (ACI) 349-13, “Code
    Requirements for Nuclear Safety-Related Concrete Structures and Commentary,” and American
    Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) 43-19, “Seismic Design Criteria for Structures, Systems, and
    Components in Nuclear Facilities.” The Hermes 2 design will use a structural system with a
    combination of cast-in-place (CIP) and precast concrete with emulative detailing.
•   Kairos stated that ASCE 43-19 does not prohibit use of precast structural walls with reliable
    seismic performance in the seismic force-resisting system and includes provisions and listed
 M. Hayes                                          3


    attributes of a system that can achieve ductile response under seismic loads, which could be
    used for emulative precast concrete to be designed and detailed to behave like CIP concrete.
•   Kairos stated that ACI 550.1 provides guidance for detailing precast concrete structures to meet
    building code requirements for seismic demands by emulating CIP reinforced concrete design.
    Kairos also stated that the National Earthquake Hazards Reduction Program (NEHRP)
    Recommended Seismic Provisions and ACI 550.1 suggest emulative detailing can be achieved
    using ductile connections or using strong connections. Kairos also stated that in implementing
    this strategy, the Hermes 2 reactor building design can include precast concrete consistent with
    industry codes and standards.
•   Kairos requested feedback from the NRC staff if there is any misalignment in its conclusions
    that this design approach is consistent with codes and standards.
•   The staff stated that they don’t object, in principle, to the use of precast concrete for a safety-
    related reactor building; however, additional information would be needed to support a future
    licensing application. This information includes the technical basis for ductility and strength of
    connection and on how the emulative concrete structures, made of precast concrete, will
    perform like a traditional CIP monolithic concrete structure. The staff stated that if mechanical
    splices are used, they should be capable of achieving the specified minimum tensile strength.
•   The staff stated that Kairos should consider making reference to ACI 550.1 in its licensing basis
    for Hermes 2 FSAR, since the concept of emulative detailing is explicitly stated in that
    document.
One member of the public commented that per ACI the use of precast walls is not permitted for
lateral seismic loads. The staff noted that the ACI code does have provisions that allow it if adequately
supported and justified, and that the staff will have to evaluate the supporting data and technical
justifications provided by Kairos.
Closed Sessions
Kairos and the NRC staff continued its discussion on the use of precast concrete during two closed
sessions because the information discussed was proprietary. The first closed session was held right
after the public session ended. A second closed session was held on April 1, 2026. Below is a
summary of those discussions.
•   Kairos presented drawings detailing wall horizontal and vertical joints, concrete, and rebar
    configuration at CIP and wet joints.
•   The staff asked if Kairos has any data regarding the performance of joints. Kairos stated that it
    is working with vendors to see what additional data they are willing to share with the NRC.
    Kairos also stated that it will be using connections that have demonstrated performance per the
    Building Code.
•   The staff stated that, during an audit for the eventual FSAR review, it would request the detailed
    joint drawings and supporting performance data. Kairos stated that it plans to have them
    available for an audit by the staff.
•   The staff noted that specific attention should be given to the licensing basis code, ACI 349-13,
    Chapter 21, “Provisions for Earthquake Resistant Design,” cross-referenced paragraphs
    21.1.1.3 and 21.1.1.4 (reproduced below), which should be complied with if precast concrete is
    used for seismic-force resisting systems. The staff noted that Kairos should address the specific
    provision (21.1.1.4) to demonstrate equivalent strength and ductility “by experimental evidence
    and analysis.”
           The staff noted that per ACI 349-13:
 M. Hayes                                          4


           21.1.1.3 The following reinforced concrete seismic-force resisting systems are permitted
           for nuclear safety-related applications:
           (a) Moment frames; and
           (b) Shear walls.
           Ordinary intermediate moment-resisting frame, intermediate moment-resisting frame,
           and precast concrete structural systems, as defined in ACI 318 [Structural concrete
           element cast elsewhere than its final position in the structure], are prohibited for use in
           the design of lateral-force-resisting systems of nuclear facilities unless the requirements
           of 21.1.1.4 are satisfied.
           21.1.1.4 A reinforced concrete structural system not satisfying the requirements of this
           chapter shall be permitted if it is demonstrated by experimental evidence and analysis
           that the proposed system will have strength and ductility equal to or exceeding that
           provided by the reinforced concrete seismic-force-resisting systems of 21.1.1.3.
•   The staff asked if Kairos has a definition of emulative concrete from the ACI 349 code
    committee and if Kairos plans to submit an inquiry to ACI 349 regarding a definition or its
    interpretation of emulative concrete. Kairos stated that the ACI 349 describes and defines
    emulative concrete. Kairos stated that it didn’t plan to submit an inquiry and that it will discuss
    this topic with the staff at a later time.
